description: Garlic Naan is a beloved Indian flatbread, soft and chewy, infused with aromatic garlic and fresh cilantro. Traditionally baked in a tandoor, this recipe brings the authentic flavors of India right to your kitchen. It is the perfect accompaniment to any rich curry or lentil dish, offering a delightful garlicky kick.

instructions.title: Activate the Yeast
instructions.text: In a small bowl, combine the warm milk (ensure it is not hot, just lukewarm), granulated sugar, and active dry yeast. Stir gently and let it sit for 5-10 minutes until a foamy layer appears on the surface, indicating that the yeast is active and ready to use.

instructions.title: Prepare the Dough
instructions.text: In a large mixing bowl, combine the all-purpose flour and salt. Add the activated yeast mixture, plain yogurt, and 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil or ghee. Mix with a spoon or your hands until a shaggy, cohesive dough starts to form.

instructions.title: Knead and First Rise
instructions.text: Transfer the dough to a lightly floured surface and knead for 7-10 minutes. The dough should become smooth, soft, and elastic. If it is too sticky, add a tiny bit more flour; if too dry, add a small amount of warm milk. Place the kneaded dough in a lightly greased bowl, turn it once to coat, then cover with a damp cloth or plastic wrap. Let it rise in a warm place for 1.5 to 2 hours, or until it has doubled in size.

instructions.title: Prepare Garlic-Cilantro Topping
instructions.text: While the naan dough is undergoing its first rise, prepare the flavorful topping. Finely mince the garlic cloves and finely chop the fresh cilantro. In a small bowl, combine the minced garlic, chopped cilantro, and the 2 tablespoons of melted butter or ghee. Stir well and set aside.

instructions.title: Shape and Cook Naan
instructions.text: Once the dough has risen, gently punch it down to release the air. Divide the dough into 6-8 equal portions. On a lightly floured surface, roll each portion into an oval or teardrop shape, about 6-8 inches long and 1/4 inch thick. Heat a cast-iron skillet or a heavy-bottomed non-stick pan over high heat until it is smoking hot. Gently place one rolled naan onto the dry hot skillet. Cook for 1-2 minutes until numerous bubbles appear on the surface.

instructions.title: Flip, Finish, and Serve
instructions.text: Flip the naan and cook on the other side for another 1-2 minutes until golden brown spots appear and it is fully cooked. For an authentic tandoor-like char, if you have a gas stove, you can use tongs to briefly hold the cooked naan directly over an open flame for a few seconds on each side. As each naan comes off the pan, immediately brush generously with the prepared garlic-cilantro butter mixture. Stack the cooked naans on a plate and cover them with a clean kitchen towel to keep them warm and soft until serving. Serve hot with your favorite Indian curries, dals, or kebabs.

tips: Ensure your milk is warm (not hot) to activate the yeast effectively; too hot will kill it, too cold will slow it down.
For a crispier naan, press it gently with a spatula while cooking on the skillet. For a softer naan, cover it immediately after brushing with butter.
Naan is best served fresh and hot. If you have leftovers, sprinkle with a little water, cover, and reheat briefly in a microwave or oven for best results.
